title: Planetary Nebula Sh2-68
caption: The planetary nebula Sh2-68, imaged by the Mayall 4-meter Telescope
credit: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA)

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: A patch of bluish gas surrounds a very blue star, while diffuse orange light spreads toward the upper right. This is Sh2-68 in Serpens Cauda, an ancient planetary nebula whose age is estimated at 45,000 years or more.
The very blue star at the center of the bluish gas is the progenitor, the star whose outer layers formed the nebula. That bluish interior glows because of energized oxygen atoms.

The orange haze to the upper right has a different origin. It comes from the nebula's movement through the disc of our galaxy, as it runs into the gas along its path. Planetary nebulae usually fade and disperse over time, so one this old offers a look at a late stage in the life of these objects, when their surroundings shape them more and more.

understand.summary: The Mayall 4-meter Telescope's Mosaic camera used two narrowband filters. Hydrogen-alpha is shown in red and oxygen [O III] in blue.
